'''Sergio Rodríguez Gómez''' ({{IPA|es|ˈseɾxjo roˈðɾiɣeθ}}; born 12 June 1986) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player who played for 21 seasons, most notably in the [[EuroLeague]], and for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the Spanish [[Liga ACB]], but also had two short stints in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Standing at {{height|m=1.91}}, he played at the [[point guard]] position. Rodriguez, nicknamed "'''El Chacho'''",<ref>{{cite web |title=Meet the New Guys: Sergio Rodriguez {{!}} Philadelphia 76ers |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/meet-new-guys-sergio-rodriguez/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=16 January 2017 |date=19 September 2016}}</ref> won the EuroLeague title [[2015 EuroLeague Final Four|in 2015]], and was an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection, as well as the [[EuroLeague MVP]] [[2013–14 Euroleague|the year before]].

Rodríguez was a regular member of the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]], with whom he won a [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]] title in [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006]], an [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympics]] silver medal in [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012]], as well as a bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]]. He also won a [[EuroBasket]] title in [[EuroBasket 2015|2015]], a silver medal in [[EuroBasket 2007|2007]], and a bronze medal in [[EuroBasket 2013|2013]]. He earned an [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-EuroBasket Team]] selection in 2015.

==Professional career==
===Estudiantes (2003–2006)===
Prior to joining the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Rodríguez was chosen to play for the 2004 World Junior Select team to play against the best high school players at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]], located in the United States. Before joining the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], Rodríguez also played professional basketball at the senior club level for [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]], in which he played a final against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] in the 2003–04 season, and won the [[ACB Rising Star Award]] for the 2004–05 season.

===Portland Trail Blazers (2006–2009)===
[[File:Portland Trail Blazers crop.jpg|thumb|left|Rodríguez with [[Portland Trail Blazers|Trail Blazers]]' teammates [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]], [[LaMarcus Aldridge]] and [[Channing Frye]] in January 2008]]
Rodríguez was selected with the 27th pick in the first round, by the [[Phoenix Suns]], in the [[2006 NBA draft]] (and later that day traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for cash considerations). On July 20, 2006, it was announced that the Trail Blazers had negotiated a buyout with his Spanish League club [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]], and signed him to an NBA rookie-scale contract.

Throughout his spell at Portland, he did not earn much playing time, primarily playing as back-up point-guard. He was sidelined by the likes of [[Jarrett Jack]] or [[Steve Blake]], who were favoured by coach [[Nate McMillan]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com.gt/basquetbol/nba/nota/_/id/2887510/sergio-rodriguez-regresa-para-vivir-el-sueno-de-la-nba |website=[[espn.com]] |title=Sergio Rodríguez regresa para vivir el sueño de la NBA |first=Adry |last=Torres |date=12 December 2016}}</ref><ref name=as>{{Cite web |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/2014/02/15/nba/1392492148_822778.html |website=[[as.com]] |title=McMillan: "Sergio Rodríguez vino demasiado joven a la NBA" |date=15 February 2014 |first=Alejandro |last=Delmás}}</ref> He developed great court chemistry with fellow Spaniard [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/202307-questions-facing-the-portland-trail-blazers |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |title=Questions Facing The Portland Trail Blazers |date=19 June 2009 |first=Nick |last=Poust}}</ref>

Rodríguez did not get along with McMillan, who had had a profile of low-risk point guard in his playing career.<ref name=sardinero /> In the view of Rodríguez, McMillan was more "unjust than just" towards him, although—conveying a mixed balance—he pointed out that McMillan still gave him some opportunities after the arrival of highly touted prospect [[Jerryd Bayless]].<ref name=sardinero>{{Cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/basket-and-roll/2012/03/21/asi-recuerda-sergio-rodriguez-a-mcmillan.html |website=[[Marca.com]] |title=Así recuerda Sergio Rodríguez a McMillan, Westphal y D'Antoni, sus tres entrenadores NBA recién despedidos |date=21 March 2012 |first=David |last=Sardinero}}</ref> Retrospectively, McMillan shared the opinion that Rodríguez had entered the NBA "too young", allegedly undeveloped as player.<ref name=as />

===Sacramento Kings and New York Knicks (2009–2010)===
On June 25, 2009, Rodríguez was traded, along with the 37th pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]], and cash considerations, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the 31st pick in the 2009 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers trade Sergio Rodriguez, Jon Brockman to Kings for Jeff Pendergraph |publisher=[[Inside Hoops|InsideHoops.com]] |date=June 25, 2010 |access-date=September 3, 2011 |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4464}}</ref> In 39 games played for the Kings, he averaged 6 points and 3.1 assists per game.

On February 18, 2010, Rodríguez was traded to the [[New York Knicks]], along with [[Tracy McGrady]], in a 3-team trade deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks obtain McGrady in 3-team, 9-player trade |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]] |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=September 3, 2011 |url=http://m.si.com/news/to/to/detail/2364062 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711054052/http://m.si.com/news/to/to/detail/2364062 |archive-date=July 11, 2012}}</ref> He appeared in 27 games for the Knicks, averaging 7.4 points and 3.4 assists per game.

===Real Madrid (2010–2016)===
[[File:Sergio Rodríguez Gómez - Real Madrid - 01.jpg|thumb|left|Rodríguez with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in May 2011]]
On July 5, 2010, after spending four seasons in the NBA, Rodríguez signed a 3-year contract with the Spanish team [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sergio Rodriguez joins Real Madrid |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008391822/noticia/Noticia/Sergio_Rodriguez_joins_Real_Madrid.htm |access-date=September 3, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100907060107/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008391822/noticia/Noticia/Sergio_Rodriguez_joins_Real_Madrid.htm |archive-date=September 7, 2010}}</ref> In July 2012, he signed a 2-year contract extension with Real Madrid, extending his contract through the 2014–15 season.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/98946/7224 Euroleague.net REAL MADRID, Rodriguez agree to extension through 2015.]</ref>

On January 9, 2014, he signed an extension with Real Madrid, staying in the club until 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sergio Rodriguez extends with Real Madrid till 2018 |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/110173/sergio-rodriguez-extends-with-real-madrid-till-2018.html |access-date=27 June 2015 |work=sportando.com |date=9 January 2014}}</ref> In May 2014, alongside his teammate [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]], he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] of the [[2013–14 Euroleague|EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2013-14 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/136869 |work=Euroleague.net |access-date=9 May 2014}}</ref> Prior to the [[2014 Euroleague Final Four|2014 Final Four]], he was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] of the season, after averaging 14 points, 4.9 assists, and 2 rebounds per game,  over 31 games played, despite not starting in any game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rodriguez voted bwin MVP of the 2013-14 Turkish Airlines Euroleague |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/137020 |work=Euroleague.net |access-date=15 May 2014}}</ref>

In the 2014–15 season, Real Madrid won the [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague]], after defeating [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], by a score of 78–59 in the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|2015 finals game]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid is Euroleague champion for record ninth time! |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2014#!report |access-date=18 July 2015 |work=euroleague.net |date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid eventually finished the season by also winning the season's [[2014–15 ACB season|Spanish League]] championship, after a 3–0 series sweep in the Spanish League's final series against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]]. With that title win, Real Madrid won the [[European Basketball Triple Crown|triple crown]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid make it 4 out of 4 |url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/06/24/en/football/real_madrid/1435176357.html |access-date=24 June 2015 |work=marca.com |date=24 June 2015 |language=es}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2016–2017)===
On 13 July 2016, Rodríguez signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-guards-bayless-and-rodriguez |title=Sixers Sign Guards Bayless and Rodriguez |work=NBA.com |date=13 July 2016 |access-date=13 July 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the 76ers in their season opener on 26 October 2016, recording 12 points and nine assists in a 103–97 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://watch.nba.com/game/20161026/OKCPHI |title=Thunder at 76ers |work=NBA.com |date=26 October 2016 |access-date=27 October 2016}}</ref> On April 8, 2017, Rodriguez was ruled out for the final three games of the season due to knee soreness after playing 68 games and starting a career high 30 games for the franchise.

===CSKA Moscow (2017–2019)===
On July 17, 2017, Rodríguez signed with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=16219&lang=en |title=Sergio Rodriguez: first Spanish player in CSKA history! |work=cskabasket.com |date=July 17, 2017 |access-date=July 17, 2017 |archive-date=17 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180417192002/https://cskabasket.com/news/?id=16219&lang=en |url-status=dead }}</ref> In May 2018, he was named the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] for the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|2017–18 season]].<ref name="all-euroleague">{{cite news |title=2017-18 All-EuroLeague Second Team presented by 7DAYS |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8qbb3a9iw6ykxips/2017-18-all-euroleague-second-team-presented-by-7days |access-date=19 May 2018 |work=euroleague.net |date=10 May 2018}}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2019–2022)===
On July 12, 2019, Rodriguez signed a three-year deal with the Italian basketball team, [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/906184/sergio-rodriguez-signs-three-year-deal-with-olimpia-milano/ |title=Sergio Rodriguez signs three-year deal with Olimpia Milano |publisher=Eurohoops.net |date=July 12, 2019 |access-date=January 9, 2020}}</ref> In his first game with Milano, Rodriguez recorded 21 points and 4 assists in a 75–53 win over the [[De' Longhi Treviso]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Italy/2019/0926_17657_4.asp |title=Treviso 53 - Milano 75 |publisher=Eurobasket |date=September 26, 2019 |access-date=January 9, 2020}}</ref> On July 2, 2022, Rodriguez amicably parted ways with the Italian club after three seasons, having also served as the team's captain.

===Return to Real Madrid (2022–2024)===
On 18 July 2022, Rodriguez returned to Real Madrid on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real brings back 'El Chacho'|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/real-brings-back-el-chacho/?pageTitle=Homepage&historyUrl=/euroleague/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=18 July 2022|access-date=18 July 2022}}</ref> On 19 June 2024, Rodríguez announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Javier|last=Gancedo|title=Three-time EuroLeague champ Sergio Rodriguez retires|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/three-time-euroleague-champ-sergio-rodriguez-retires/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=19 June 2024|access-date=1 July 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Sergio Rodríguez.jpg|thumb|right|Rodríguez with the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]] in 2012]]
Thought to be one of the best European prospects of his age, Rodríguez was named the MVP of the [[2004 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], which was held in [[Zaragoza]], Spain, while playing with the Spain national junior team. He led the host Spanish team to the tournament's gold medal. In the eight games of that tournament, he averaged 19 points per game, 4.6 rebounds per game, 8.5 assists per game, and 2.1 steals per game.

In August 2006, Rodríguez won the gold medal at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], while playing with the senior men's [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]]. He also won the silver medal with Spain's senior national team at the [[EuroBasket 2007]]. In 2012, he won a silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Summer Olympics]] in London. In 2016, he won a bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Summer Olympic Games]] in Rio de Janeiro.

Rodríguez decided to skip the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 World Cup]], citing a need to rest.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/baloncesto/abci-sergio-rodriguez-renuncia-mundial-sentido-necesidad-parar-201907091115_noticia.html |website=[[ABC (Spain)|ABC]] |title=Sergio Rodríguez renuncia al Mundial: "He sentido la necesidad de parar" |date=9 July 2019}}</ref> He was called up by Sergio Scariolo for the [[2020 Summer Olympics]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://es.nba.com/news/plantilla-12-jugadores-seleccion-espanola-juegos-olimpicos-de-tokio-2020/gs0kvsggp4pj1izpjfl7syxx3 |website=[[nba.com]] |title=Sergio Scariolo confirma los 12 jugadores de la Selección española para los Juegos Olímpicos de Tokio 2020 |date=24 July 2021 |first=Sergio |last=Rabinal}}</ref> celebrated in 2021.

== Player profile ==
Possessing a knack for [[pick and roll]] plays,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2015/06/27/sergio-rodriguez-is-mulling-a-return-to-the-nba/ |website=[[NBC Sports]] |title=Sergio Rodriguez is mulling a return to the NBA |first=Brett |last=Pollakoff |date=Jun 27, 2015}}</ref> Rodríguez was known for feeding his teammates with [[alley-oop]]s and creative passing.<ref name="euroleague">{{Cite web |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/albfc5kntfosv7f7/signature-moves-sergio-rodriguez |website=[[Euroleague.net]] |title=Signature Moves: Sergio Rodriguez |date=13 May 2020}}</ref> His style of play has drawn comparisons to former NBA player [[Jason Williams (basketball, born 1975)|Jason Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://hoopshabit.com/2015/06/28/sergio-rodriguez-blazers-reunite/ |website=Hoops Habit |title=Should Sergio Rodriguez And The Blazers Reunite? |first=Chris |last=St. Jean |date=28 June 2015}}</ref> He maintained a high assist-to-turnover ratio and also excelled as scorer, posting high 3-point and free-throw percentages throughout his career.<ref name=euroleague />

== Post-retirement ==
Rodríguez was appointed sporting director of basketball at Real Madrid in July 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-sergio-rodriguez-02-07-2025 |title=Official Announcement: Sergio Rodríguez |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=2 July 2025 }}</ref> He stepped down from his position in June 2026 following a trophyless season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://basketnews.com/news-250093-sergio-rodriguez-steps-down-as-real-madrid-basketball-sporting-director.html |title=Sergio Rodriguez steps down as Real Madrid basketball sporting director |publisher=Basketnews |date=19 June 2026 }}</ref>
